text: In this article United Airlines said on Wednesday it would restrict AI bots' access to its ⁠digital platforms, citing data security, in the latest pushback ​against AI agents ​increasingly capable ​of planning and booking trips for travelers. Companies across industries ⁠are ‌taking divergent approaches to the ⁠rapid rise of AI agents capable of carrying out tasks on behalf of users — some restricting access ‌to protect their platforms, others embracing partnerships. Amazon has blocked Meta's AI ​agent Muse, while Walmart has partnered with it. Meanwhile, online travel firms such as Expedia and Booking are working ⁠with ChatGPT-parent OpenAI. United warned that sharing ‌account credentials with third-party AI ‌assistants could expose sensitive information and lead to unintended purchases, account modifications or the unauthorized use ⁠of frequent-flyer miles. It also said automated ⁠AI tools performing actions like flight ⁠check-in — which requires human acknowledgment for prohibited items such as explosives — could ​create regulatory risks. The ‌carrier said it would take steps to restrict access both directly through its digital platforms and indirectly through travel agencies and aggregators, including ​updates to its booking, ticketing ‌and distribution policies.
